definition.given: A signed-in administrator has two interfaces, uplink0 on Akron Edge A and Akron Edge B. A cable previously connected them and was subsequently deleted through the application's cable-deletion action. The browser starts on the filtered interface list.
definition.when: Open Akron Edge A's uplink0 interface, inspect its Connection panel, open its Changelog, and open the latest interface-update entry to inspect the recorded connection change.
definition.observed: The current interface detail says Not Connected. Its complete four-entry Changelog includes creation, the connection update, and a related Cable Termination deletion, but no later interface update recording the disconnect. The latest interface-update detail shows cable changing from null to the now-deleted cable ID, with cable_end becoming A. This older connection entry is valid history; the defect is the missing subsequent disconnect record, not incorrect live connection state or corruption of the earlier event.
definition.require: In the interface's own Changelog, expose a later disconnection event. Opening it must explain the connected cable and cable-end assignment being cleared. Keep the interface disconnected and preserve the earlier connection event.
allow: A normal interface-update entry or an equivalent interface-associated disconnect event is acceptable if it is discoverable in that interface's Changelog and exposes the before-and-after connection state.
Numeric cable identifiers, readable cable descriptions, structured data, or a readable diff may convey the transition; exact IDs, field rendering, wording, colors, and row counts are not prescribed.

Related Cable Termination deletion entries may remain alongside the disconnect event. An older connection event may still show its original cable; it must not be rewritten to represent the later deletion.

theory.title: Command History: reviewable records of meaningful operations
theory.reference: Jenifer Tidwell, Charles Brewer, and Aynne Valencia, Designing Interfaces, Third Edition; Chapter 8: Actions and Commands. Conceptual application based on chapter synthesis.
theory.rationale: A reviewable history must represent meaningful changes at the level the person is inspecting. Cable deletion changes the interface connection state; recording only a related termination deletion leaves the interface history unable to explain how its present disconnected state followed its earlier connection. This application of the pattern requires a reviewable disconnect record, not undo, replay, or a particular logging implementation.

reference_observation: The disconnected interface's Changelog contains a later interface update showing cable and cable_end changing from their connected values to null. The earlier connection event remains available with its original historical values.
requirement_rationale: Deleting a cable changes the attached interface as well as the cable object. Its history needs to explain that transition to the current disconnected state without rewriting the earlier connection.
